name: Copywriter
seoDescription: Calculate estimated business insurance costs for copywriter businesses including general liability and professional E&O coverage.

industryContext.contextNote: Copywriters produce written content with no physical work product or premises risk, so their exposure is almost entirely tied to the accuracy and originality of the words they deliver.

riskFactors.title: Missed Deadlines & Scope Disputes
riskFactors.description: Late or incomplete deliverables can trigger breach-of-contract claims from clients relying on copy for time-sensitive campaigns.

riskFactors.title: Copyright & Plagiarism Claims
riskFactors.description: Content that unintentionally mirrors existing copyrighted material can expose both the writer and the client to infringement claims.

riskFactors.title: Misleading Claims in Client Copy
riskFactors.description: Marketing copy that overstates a client's product claims can create liability if a third party relies on inaccurate statements.

faqs.question: Why do copywriters need Errors & Omissions insurance?
faqs.answer: E&O coverage protects copywriters against claims that their content was inaccurate, plagiarized, or failed to meet contractual expectations, which General Liability alone does not address.

faqs.question: What is the average cost of business insurance for a copywriter?
faqs.answer: A solo copywriter in the $0-50k revenue tier pays an estimated $245 per year for baseline General Liability coverage, one of the lowest tiers in the business-insurance calculator.

faqs.question: Does a copywriter need General Liability if they work from home?
faqs.answer: Most copywriters carry General Liability primarily because clients require proof of coverage in contracts, even though in-person client interaction is rare.

faqs.question: Is copyright infringement covered by standard business insurance?
faqs.answer: Some E&O and media liability endorsements cover unintentional infringement claims, but coverage varies by carrier, so copywriters should confirm this explicitly with their policy.

blogContent.whyThisRiskFactor: Copywriters hold a 0.8 actuarial risk factor, among the lowest in the calculator, reflecting minimal physical hazard and narrow professional-liability exposure.
blogContent.howCalculated: Premiums scale with annual revenue tier and team size, with Professional Liability (E&O) as the primary optional endorsement.
blogContent.comparisonNote: Copywriting premiums are among the lowest of any profession modeled here, comparable to graphic designers and translators, and well below hands-on trades or hospitality businesses.
